saints.name: Sts. Andrew Kim Taegŏn, Paul Chŏng Hasang, and Companions
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: The first Korean priest, a lay catechist, and a great company of Korean Christians who kept the faith through waves of persecution unto death…
biography: The Church in Korea was founded largely by lay believers and grew under fierce persecution through the nineteenth century. Among its martyrs Andrew Kim Taegŏn, the first native Korean priest, was beheaded in 1846, and Paul Chŏng Hasang, a lay catechist who long petitioned for missionary clergy, was put to death in 1839.

With them the Church honours one hundred and three martyrs — bishops, priests, and above all lay men, women, and children — who died rather than renounce Christ. They were canonized together by Pope John Paul II in Seoul in 1984.
saints.knownFor: The witness of the Korean martyrs and the faith planted by lay believers.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of the Martyrs of Korea (vatican.va)
